messages:
Maya: quick sync — need to lock scope for the observability console work for Q2. Two high-priority customer asks: per-route cost breakdown (tokens -> $) and actionable error analytics for inference failures. We also need tracing hooks to support the error flows. Can we surface engineering bounds + acceptance gates today?
Tony: I can give high-level eng bounds. Dashboards + cost explorer: ~3 sprint tasks (backend + queries + UI). Tracing envelope + sampling impl: ~2 sprints if we reuse runtime hooks. Biggest unknown: per-request cost attribution accuracy and aggregation pipeline ops.
Zara: SRE note — tracing hooks can blow up cardinality and ingestion costs. We should default to envelope-level telemetry (not full spans) and async export. Suggest sampling default 0.1% prod, 100% on canary.
Sophie: from design: MVP should be 1) summary dashboard, 2) cost-explorer with quick filters (model, route, customer), 3) error analytics panel with top error types. Keep charts minimal. Avoid multi-page dashboards at launch.
Eli: customers want alerts when per-route cost or error-rate jumps. Acceptance criteria should include alerts + runbook + a simple CSV export for billing reconciliation.
Tony: implementation note: runtime can emit a compact trace envelope. Example payload we can instrument today:
```json
{
  "trace_id": "<uuid>",
  "model": "gpt-j-16k",
  "route": "generate/text",
  "tokens": 124,
  "gpu_ms": 42,
  "error": null
}
```
Zara: that envelope looks safe. Export path should be async -> queue -> telemetry pipeline. Add a sample_rate field to make sampling explicit. Also enforce redaction before export.
Maya: tradeoff decision proposal: MVP = envelope-only (no full-span captures), default sample_rate=0.1% in prod, canary 100%. Surface per-route estimated $/1000 tokens in UI rather than attempting perfect accounting. Agree?
Tony: agree. For cost model we'll compute cost = tokens * per_token_cost + infra_overhead and surface estimate. Need to add batching and aggregation so we don't emit per-token metrics at high volume.
Eli: propose gating metrics for GA: 1) dashboard shows last 24h of data for baseline routes; 2) canary tracing envelope processing latency <5s end-to-end; 3) cost estimate error <10% on sample workload; 4) alerts firing correctly on simulated spikes.
Sophie: UX acceptance: filter state persistence, quick CSV export, and a compact error drilldown with top 5 errors + sample payload. Those are low-effort but high-value.
Maya: action items: Tony -> eng plan + break down + EOD estimate; Zara -> sampling + export perf test plan; Sophie -> dashboard mockups for minimal drilldowns; Eli -> customer comms & canary list. I'll own acceptance gating doc. Sync at 10:30 PT. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: heads-up: new telemetry pipeline quota enforcement starts 2026-04-01. Check quotas here: https://internal.redwood/telemetry-quotas
Tony: noted — will include quota-aware fallback (batching, aggregated metrics, and backpressure).
Zara: one more acceptance: error analytics must include top-5 stack traces and a single redacted payload sample per error type. We must verify PII redaction before export.
Maya: good catch. Final scope lock for MVP: dashboards (summary + cost-explorer + CSV), tracing envelope (sampled, async), error analytics (top5 + redacted payload samples), alerts + runbook. If anyone sees a hard blocker, ping me ASAP. Thanks everyone.
